visual.general_description: Black-and-white flowchart titled "Management of hypertriglyceridemia in HTGAP" that branches into "Diabetes" and "No Diabetes" boxes, converges on a shared monitoring box, then a triglyceride recheck after 12 hours with two outcome branches, a 12-hourly triglyceride box and a final "Prior to discharge" box.
visual.detailed_description: Rounded rectangles joined by downward arrows on a white background. The top box reads "Management of hypertriglyceridemia in HTGAP" and two arrows lead to two small boxes, "Diabetes" and "No Diabetes". Under "Diabetes" a numbered box lists: 1. Intravenous insulin infusion starting rate 0.05 units/kg/hour; 2. Give usual long acting subcutaneous insulin; 3. Withhold oral hypoglycaemic agents. Under "No Diabetes" a numbered box lists: 1. Discuss with Endocrine team; 2. Consider intravenous insulin infusion recommend starting rate 0.03 units/kg/hour. Arrows from both boxes enter one wide box with six numbered items: 1. Hourly blood glucose level (BGL); 2. Start intravenous dextrose** once BGL < 10 mmol/L; 3. Target BGL 5-10 mmol/L; 4. 2-hourly venous blood gas - replace potassium aim 4-5 mmol/L; 5. Nil by mouth then low fat <30g/day diet (timing of oral intake after discussion with surgical team); 6. Commence deep venous thrombosis prophylaxis unless contraindicated. The same box ends with "**NOTE: Initial resuscitation and maintenance fluids will be in accordance with routine standard of care as per treating surgical team." An arrow leads to "Recheck triglyceride levels after 12 hours", which splits into "Triglyceride level >20% fall from admission" and "Triglyceride level <20% fall from admission". The first leads to "Continue insulin/ dextrose/ potassium/ dietary management"; the second leads to a box listing 1. Increase insulin infusion rate to 0.1units/kg/hour; 2. Titrate IV dextrose to maintain BGL 5-10 mmol/L; 3. Ongoing potassium replacement. Both lead to a box with 1. 12-hourly Triglyceride levels; 2. Stop insulin and dextrose infusions when Triglyceride level <5.6mmol/L. The last box, "Prior to discharge,", lists 1. Commence fenofibrate +/- statin +/- omega-3; 2. Lifestyle modification with a. Dietary: avoid alcohol, fructose, and high fat food and b. Encourage physical activity; 3. For those with diabetes, medical optimisation of glycaemic control; 4. Re-check triglyceride level at 6 weeks and 6 months. No patient identifiers, dates or measured patient values are printed.

visual.general_description: Four line charts, one per case (Case 1, Case 6, Case 9 and Case 10), each plotting a triglyceride series and a daily insulin requirement series against day labels.
visual.detailed_description: Two-by-two grid of light-bordered chart panels on a white background titled "Case 1", "Case 6", "Case 9" and "Case 10". Each panel has a blue line with markers labelled "Triglyceride (mmol/l)" on the left y-axis titled "Triglyceride level" and an orange line with markers labelled "Insulin (Units/day)" on the right y-axis titled "Daily insulin requirements". Day labels from Day 1 AM onward run along the x-axis of each panel. In Case 1, Case 9 and Case 10 the blue line declines overall; in Case 6 it rises over the first markers and then declines. The orange insulin series rises and then falls or fluctuates in every panel. No data labels, patient identifiers or dates are printed.
